global_organization_chain: Summary chain: overtaking-rule task -> lane-change mechanism -> ring-road cellular automaton -> nine-rule criteria -> regime-specific choice -> transfer and ramps.
Restatement chain: simulate overtaking -> expose changeable inputs and mechanisms -> collect outputs -> combine flow, safety, and experience -> choose a rule.
Literature chain: single-lane cellular automaton -> multi-lane safety and incentive -> heterogeneous vehicles -> expectation-aware extension.
Overview chain: microscopic trigger model -> periodic multi-lane automaton -> open-boundary ramp refinement -> standard-model experiments.
Lane-change chain: desire to pass -> rear safety -> front opportunity -> left maneuver -> return-right constraints.
Algorithm chain: state and vehicle type -> acceleration -> randomization -> safety deceleration -> motion -> lane-change test -> next state.
Boundary chain: constant-count periodic road -> controlled occupancy -> light/heavy comparison -> open-boundary ramp handoff.
Factor-results chain: define traffic regimes -> define criteria -> vary one factor -> compare plots -> state regime-specific effect.
Rule-results chain: define operational alternatives -> inspect single criteria -> weight variation -> aggregate distance -> choose by regime.
Sensitivity chain: uncertain parameter -> plus-or-minus range -> metric response table -> local robustness statement.
Extension chain: new driving orientation or controller -> changed willingness parameter -> mechanism -> simulation output -> conditional transfer.
Ramp chain: open-boundary model -> vary exit propensity -> flow, speed, lane-use, and failure outputs -> heavy/light distinction.
Final chain: practical model strengths -> behavioral and calibration weaknesses -> references and reproducibility boundary.
The final warning pass records type, notation, algorithm, data, claim, stochastic, and reproducibility defects without replacing positive learning.

main_argument_chains.claim: A traffic policy question becomes inspectable when lane-change behavior is translated into ordered cellular-automaton laws and typed metrics.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Reuse the model interface only with explicit conflict handling, calibration, stochastic design, and boundaries.

main_argument_chains.claim: Traffic regime is a necessary condition for interpreting factor effects and preferred overtaking rules.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Do not present one rule as globally optimal outside its density, criterion, and simulation scope.

main_argument_chains.claim: Sensitivity and transfer scenarios remain conditional until stochastic uncertainty and field calibration are supplied.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Report these as scenario evidence rather than external policy validation.

warnings.warning: The printed right-front opportunity condition repeats the right-rear gap symbol; reconcile it with the notation table and Figure 2 before reuse.
The relative-deviation formula prints u_0i while the criterion-indexed ideal vector implies u_0j; the unresolved Table ?? reference and denominator indexing also require reconciliation.
The printed weight denominator is extraction-flattened; retain the normalized five-criterion form only as a source-checked interpretation, not a silent source correction.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: The left-lane schematic fixes the subject vehicle, nearby vehicles, and gap directions used by the trigger and safety inequalities.
The return-right schematic distinguishes right-front and right-rear vehicles for the printed conditions.
The cellular-automaton flowchart makes the movement and lane-changing decision order inspectable.
The freeway photograph anchors the exit-before-entrance ramp geometry used by the refined model.
Time-space diagrams contrast unconstrained high-speed traces with congested low-speed traces for the light/heavy distinction.
Occupancy sweeps compare flow, speed, lane utilization, braking, shifting, satisfaction, and speed variability for three and four lanes.
Paired light/heavy plots expose the effects of maximum limits, minimum limits, and signaling across traffic metrics.
Basic-rule plots compare flow, speed, braking, satisfaction, and speed variability before aggregation.
The criterion table, ideal vector, relative-deviation matrix, and weight vector expose the multi-criteria calculation inputs.
The basic-rule deviation tables make the light/heavy preference reversal directly scannable.
The nine-rule table places light, heavy, and unexplained overall deviations beside the final recommendations.
Sensitivity tables show signed metric changes for three parameter groups across both traffic regimes.
Intelligent-system plots compare baseline, semi-intelligent, and complete control for flow, speed, braking, shifting, and lane use.
Ramp plots trace p_exit against flow, average speed, lane utilization, and failure ratio in light and heavy traffic.
